profile.reading: QTS Richmond 2 (RIC2) is a data center campus in Sandston, Virginia, just east of Richmond and immediately adjacent to Richmond International Airport, developed by QTS Realty Trust (formerly Quality Technology Services, renamed following the company's 2013 IPO; this registry tracks both names as the same operator). Per QTS's own site, the campus spans approximately 85 acres and is planned to include five buildings once fully built out, with a total planned capacity of 180 megawatts of IT power upon completion; that figure describes the campus as a whole rather than any single building, and much of it was not yet in operation as of the source page, so it is not applied here as this building's own confirmed capacity. This building, DC2, sits at 6040 Technology Boulevard, one of five addressed buildings running along Technology Boulevard: 6030 (DC1), 6040 (DC2), 6050 (DC3), 6060 (DC5), and 6070 (DC6); the campus's own numbering skips DC4 entirely, a naming gap this registry notes rather than attempts to explain. RIC2 is QTS's second Richmond-area campus, distinct from the company's original Richmond 1 (RIC1) campus elsewhere in the metro, which this registry documents as a separate set of facilities. Henrico County, where Sandston sits, has become one of the mid-Atlantic's fastest-growing data center corridors in recent years, drawing hyperscale and colocation development on the strength of available land, Dominion Energy transmission capacity, and dense regional fiber routes running through the Richmond area. QTS's own campus page does not state which, if any, of the five RIC2 buildings are currently operating versus still under construction, and does not publish individual square footage, IT capacity, or year-opened figures for any single building on the campus; none of those figures is asserted here for DC2 specifically, consistent with this registry's practice of reporting only what the operator has actually confirmed at the building level.

reading.body:
QTS Richmond 2 is a planned data center campus in Sandston, Virginia, east of Richmond and adjacent to Richmond International Airport. The operator has published a target of 180 megawatts of IT power across five buildings on approximately 85 acres once the campus is fully built out, but the operator's own specifications do not state which buildings are currently operating, under construction, or planned, and do not publish IT capacity figures for individual buildings including DC2. This reading does not apply the 180 megawatt figure to DC2 specifically because it describes the entire multi-building campus upon completion, much of which was not yet operating at the time the operator published the specification.

Henrico County has become a data center corridor on the strength of available land, Dominion Energy transmission capacity, and regional fiber routes. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 have published power capacity totaling 1,375 megawatts. The planned 180-megawatt RIC2 campus, if completed as specified, would rank as the state's 24th largest published facility or campus, though this ranking reflects a planned rather than operating figure and sits below the threshold of published capacity in current operation.

The operator has not published certifications, power delivery details, cooling technology, or any environmental or resilience rating for this campus. Whether RIC2 matters to AI scaling depends on whether and when the five planned buildings come online and at what utilization rate, neither of which the operator has disclosed.
